Deployment Overview

Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure

Complete deployment guide for on-premises Proxmox + AWS hybrid environment with FreeIPA identity, HashiCorp Vault secrets, and Kubernetes orchestration.

🎯 Interactive Documentation
This guide is fully interactive - everything is clickable!

Deployment Sequence

⚠️ Critical Order
Follow these guides in order. Each step depends on the previous ones being complete. Skipping steps will cause failures.

Infrastructure Prerequisites:

0. Network → 1. Proxmox → 2. AWS Bootstrap → 3. GitHub → 4. AWS Secrets

Core & Service Layer:

5. VPN → 6. Ansible → 7. FreeIPA ★ → 8. Vault + 9. K8s

Integration Layer:

10. Vault-K8s Trust → 11. Nginx Proxy

★ FreeIPA is the critical dependency - ALL services depend on it for DNS and Kerberos authentication

💡 Architecture Decision
Servers connect svc0 DIRECTLY to router ports (bypassing switch). Switch is only used for isolated storage network (VLAN 40). This reduces failure points after encountering USB-Ethernet adapter instability issues.

See: troubleshooting/network/ cases 43, 48, 57

Environment Isolation

Network Isolation
  • Prod VLANs (50-55) and Dev VLANs (60-65) are completely separated
  • Cross-environment traffic blocked at router firewall
  • Each environment has its own FreeIPA DNS server
Storage Isolation
  • VLAN 40 is L2-isolated on the switch (no router routing)
  • NAS, Prod stor0, Dev stor0 communicate directly
  • Storage traffic never touches the router
WiFi Isolation
  • AP Isolation enabled - WiFi clients cannot reach each other
  • Prod and Dev cannot communicate directly via WiFi
  • All inter-server traffic must go through router

Network Troubleshooting Reference

Click any case to expand full diagnosis and resolution

Case 43 Switch port link flapping ▶
Symptoms
  • Network connection dropping randomly every few minutes
  • Switch port LEDs blinking off/on
  • VMs losing connectivity intermittently
  • dmesg showing link down/up events
Root Cause
Switch port PHY instability when connecting trunk ports with many VLANs. The managed switch was overloaded processing VLAN tags.
Resolution

Bypassed switch for service traffic - connected servers directly to router ports:

Router Port 5 → Prod server svc0 (direct) Router Port 6 → Dev server svc0 (direct)

Switch now only handles storage VLAN 40 traffic.

Prevention
Keep trunk ports on capable L3 devices (router). Use switches only for simple L2 traffic.
📁 See: troubleshooting/network/3-switch-port4-link-flapping-loose-connection.md
Case 48 ER605 Port 4 PHY failure ▶
Symptoms
  • Port 4 on TP-Link ER605 stopped negotiating link
  • LED stayed dark even with cable connected
  • Worked on other ports, cable tested good
Root Cause
Hardware PHY failure on Port 4 of the ER605 router. Eventually migrated to MikroTik due to multiple ER605 issues.
Resolution

Migrated connection to different port initially. Eventually replaced ER605 with MikroTik L009UiGS-RM for more reliable hardware and better RouterOS features.

📁 See: troubleshooting/network/4-er605-port4-gigabit-negotiation.md
Case 57 USB adapter Gigabit instability ▶
Symptoms
  • USB-Ethernet adapter dropping connection under load
  • High CPU usage on USB controller
  • NFS timeouts from storage network
  • Adapter heating up significantly
Root Cause
USB 3.0 Gigabit adapters struggle to maintain stable 1Gbps under sustained load. USB bandwidth contention and thermal throttling.
Resolution

Force 100Mbps negotiation on storage ports to reduce heat and instability:

# On MikroTik for ports connecting USB adapters /interface ethernet set stor0-port speed=100M full-duplex=yes

This is acceptable for storage network as NFS doesn't need full Gigabit for our workloads.

Prevention
Use native Ethernet ports for high-bandwidth traffic. Reserve USB adapters for low-bandwidth management networks.
📁 See: troubleshooting/network/9-svc-network-instability-force-100m.md

Proxmox Installation
Boot from ISO and complete initial setup
Boot from ISO

Boot from: proxmox-ve_9.x.iso

During installation:

  • Name interfaces as: svc0 (main ethernet), stor0 (USB-Ethernet), keep WiFi name
  • Set temporary IP for initial access
  • Complete installation and reboot
Initial Access

Use any connected ethernet port or temporary network for initial SSH access.

2
Bootstrap Proxmox
Run bootstrap script to configure system

Copy and Run Bootstrap Script

bootstrap.sh 
scp proxmox/bootstrap_proxmox/bootstrap.sh root@<temp-ip>:/tmp/
ssh root@<temp-ip>
chmod +x /tmp/bootstrap.sh && /tmp/bootstrap.sh dev   # or prod

What bootstrap.sh Does

  • Disables sleep/suspend/hibernate
  • Adds fallback DNS (8.8.8.8)
  • Disables enterprise repos, enables no-subscription repo
  • APT update & upgrade
  • Removes subscription nag popup
  • Configures Chrony NTP + timezone
  • Creates admin user (admin_dev or admin_prod)
  • Creates Terraform user (tf_dev or tf_prod) with API token
🔑 Save API Token
IMPORTANT: Save the API token output from bootstrap.sh. This token will be stored in AWS Secrets Manager later.

Format: {"token_id":"tf_dev@pve!terraform","token_secret":"xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx"}
3
Network Setup
Configure WiFi, VLANs, and bridges
⚠️ Warning
Run from console or storage network, NOT over WiFi (it will disconnect you).
network-setup.sh 
scp proxmox/bootstrap_proxmox/network-setup.sh root@<ip>:/tmp/
ssh root@<ip>
chmod +x /tmp/network-setup.sh
WIFI_PASSWORD="xxx" /tmp/network-setup.sh dev   # or prod

What network-setup.sh Does

  • Installs wpa_supplicant and wireless-tools
  • Configures WiFi for unified_mgmt SSID
  • Tests WiFi connectivity
  • Configures /etc/network/interfaces (WiFi, vmbr0, vmbr1)
  • Updates /etc/hosts
  • Regenerates Proxmox SSL certificate

Foundation / AWS Bootstrap

AWS Bootstrap & IAM Step 2

⚠️ ONE-TIME Setup
This is the VERY FIRST AWS setup step. Deploy bootstrap stack BEFORE creating any secrets or running any workflows. Must be deployed by AWS root user.

Multi-Account Structure

EnvironmentRegionAdmin User
Developmentus-east-1admin_dev
Productioneu-west-2admin_prod

Note: Dev uses us-east-1 for cost optimization. Prod uses eu-west-2 for lower latency.

2-Tier IAM Role System

TIER 1: CloudFormation Bootstrap (Manual Deploy)
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  GitHubActions-TerraformAdmin-{env}                  │
│  - Trusted Branch: {env}-security                    │
│  - Policy: AdministratorAccess                       │
│  - Constraint: PermissionsBoundary                   │
│  - Purpose: IAM/security changes only                │
└────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘
                         │
                         │ Creates via Terraform
                         ▼
TIER 2: Terraform-Managed Roles
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  GitHubActions-Infrastructure-{env}                  │
│  - Trusted Branch: {env}                             │
│  - Policies: PowerUserAccess + SecurityBoundary      │
│  - Purpose: Infrastructure deployments               │
│  - Restriction: NO IAM mutation allowed              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
💡 Why 2-tier?
TerraformAdmin (Tier 1): Full admin but protected by PermissionsBoundary, only for security branch
Infrastructure (Tier 2): Day-to-day infra deployments, cannot touch IAM/CloudTrail/Billing
1
Deploy Bootstrap Stack
CloudFormation deployment (ONE-TIME)

CloudFormation Templates

AccountTemplate FileRegionStack Name
Devaws/deployment-stacks/bootstrap-dev.yamlus-east-1bootstrap-dev
Prodaws/deployment-stacks/bootstrap-prod.yamleu-west-2bootstrap-prod

Resources Created

  • GitHub OIDC Provider - Identity federation for GitHub Actions
  • TerraformPermissionsBoundary - Protects bootstrap resources
  • S3 State Bucket - Terraform state (versioned, encrypted)
  • DynamoDB Lock Table - State locking (deletion protected)
  • TerraformAdmin Role - Admin role for security branch
  • Admin User - GUI admin with billing access

Deploy via AWS Console (Recommended)

Login to AWS Console as root user
Must be deployed by AWS root user (account owner email), not IAM users.
Navigate to CloudFormation
CloudFormation → Stacks → Create stack
Upload template
Select "Upload a template file" and upload bootstrap-{env}.yaml
Configure and create
Stack name: bootstrap-{env}
Check "I acknowledge that AWS CloudFormation might create IAM resources"

Deploy via CLI

AWS CLI 
# Dev (us-east-1)
aws cloudformation deploy --template-file aws/deployment-stacks/bootstrap-dev.yaml \
    --stack-name bootstrap-dev --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM \
    --region us-east-1

# Prod (eu-west-2)
aws cloudformation deploy --template-file aws/deployment-stacks/bootstrap-prod.yaml \
    --stack-name bootstrap-prod --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM \
    --region eu-west-2

Post-Bootstrap: Enable IAM Billing Access

Sign in as root user
Go to Account settings
Account (top-right dropdown) → Account
Enable billing access
Scroll to "IAM User and Role Access to Billing Information" → Edit → Check "Activate IAM Access" → Update

Security Features

State Bucket Security
  • Versioning: Enabled (90-day retention)
  • Encryption: AES256 server-side
  • Public Access: Completely blocked
  • TLS: Enforced via bucket policy
  • DeletionPolicy: Retain
DynamoDB Lock Table
  • DeletionProtectionEnabled: true
  • SSE: Server-side encryption enabled
  • DeletionPolicy: Retain

Core Layer / WireGuard VPN

WireGuard VPN Step 5

⚠️ Prerequisite
VPN setup requires AWS Network deployed first, as the EC2 instance needs the VPC, subnets, and route tables.

VPN Tunnel Overview

Home/Datacenter (10.0.x.x)
        │
   MikroTik Router
   (172.16.200.1 dev)
   (172.17.200.1 prod)
        │
        ├──── WireGuard (UDP 51830) ────▶ AWS Dev EC2 (172.16.200.2)
        │                                        │
        │                                   AWS Dev VPC
        │                                   172.16.0.0/16
        │
        └──── WireGuard (UDP 51831) ────▶ AWS Prod EC2 (172.17.200.2)
                                                 │
                                            AWS Prod VPC
                                            172.17.0.0/16

Tunnel Summary

EnvironmentMikroTik Tunnel IPAWS Tunnel IPMikroTik PortAWS Port
Dev172.16.200.1172.16.200.25183051820
Prod172.17.200.1172.17.200.25183151820
💡 Routing Design
Tunnel IPs are within AWS VPC CIDR so one AllowedIPs entry covers both tunnel AND VPC traffic. Dev: 172.16.200.x within 172.16.0.0/16

Environment Segmentation

  • Dev VPN (172.16.x.x) can only reach Dev VLANs (60-65)
  • Prod VPN (172.17.x.x) can only reach Prod VLANs (50-55)
  • Cross-environment traffic is blocked by MikroTik firewall

Configure WireGuard on EC2
Run setup script after EC2 is deployed

SSH Config (Recommended)

~/.ssh/config 
Host wg-dev
    HostName <DEV_ELASTIC_IP>
    User ec2-user
    IdentityFile ~/WorkSpace/vpn-key-pair-dev.pem

Host wg-prod
    HostName <PROD_ELASTIC_IP>
    User ec2-user
    IdentityFile ~/WorkSpace/vpn-key-pair-prod.pem

Run Setup Script

Setup Commands 
scp network/vpn/setup-wireguard.sh wg-dev:~/
ssh wg-dev
chmod +x setup-wireguard.sh
./setup-wireguard.sh dev   # or prod

What setup-wireguard.sh Does

  • Sets hostname (wg-dev or wg-prod)
  • Generates WireGuard key pair
  • Displays AWS public key (copy for MikroTik)
  • Prompts for MikroTik public key
  • Creates /etc/wireguard/wg0.conf
  • Starts wg-quick@wg0 service
  • Creates wg-keepalive service (continuous ping)
🔑 Save Keys
The script displays the AWS public key. Copy this for the MikroTik peer configuration in the next step.
4
Configure MikroTik WireGuard
Router-side VPN configuration

Create WireGuard Interfaces

MikroTik CLI 
/interface wireguard
add comment="Dev AWS tunnel" listen-port=51830 mtu=1420 name=dev-tunnel
add comment="Prod AWS tunnel" listen-port=51831 mtu=1420 name=prod-tunnel

Assign Tunnel IPs

MikroTik CLI 
/ip address
add address=172.16.200.1/16 interface=dev-tunnel network=172.16.0.0
add address=172.17.200.1/16 interface=prod-tunnel network=172.17.0.0

Configure Peers

MikroTik CLI 
/interface wireguard peers
add allowed-address=172.16.0.0/16 comment="AWS Dev" \
    endpoint-address=<AWS_DEV_EIP> endpoint-port=51820 \
    interface=dev-tunnel persistent-keepalive=10s \
    public-key="<AWS_DEV_PUBLIC_KEY>"

add allowed-address=172.17.0.0/16 comment="AWS Prod" \
    endpoint-address=<AWS_PROD_EIP> endpoint-port=51820 \
    interface=prod-tunnel persistent-keepalive=10s \
    public-key="<AWS_PROD_PUBLIC_KEY>"

Add Routes & Firewall

MikroTik CLI 
/ip route
add comment="AWS Dev VPC" dst-address=172.16.0.0/16 gateway=dev-tunnel
add comment="AWS Prod VPC" dst-address=172.17.0.0/16 gateway=prod-tunnel

/ip firewall filter
add action=accept chain=input comment="WireGuard Dev" dst-port=51830 \
    in-interface=ether1 protocol=udp
add action=accept chain=input comment="WireGuard Prod" dst-port=51831 \
    in-interface=ether1 protocol=udp

Verification Commands

On AWS EC2

EC2 Commands 
sudo wg show                        # WireGuard status
sudo systemctl status wg-keepalive  # Keepalive service
ping 172.16.200.1                   # Test tunnel (dev)

On MikroTik

MikroTik Commands 
/interface wireguard peers print    # Show peers
/ping 172.16.200.2                  # Test tunnel (dev)

Ansible & Local Runner Step 6

⚠️ Critical Order
Ansible and Local Runner must be deployed BEFORE FreeIPA. All subsequent workflows run via these nodes.

Architecture Overview

GitHub Actions (mac-mini runner)

   10.0.63.10            │

Why Two Nodes?

  • Ansible LXC: Stores repo (/srv/repo), runs playbooks, has Ansible vault password
  • Local Runner: GitHub Actions runner for workflows needing local network access
  • Local Runner SSHs to Ansible to execute playbooks
  • Runner service runs as "runner" user (not root)

Integration Layer / Vault-K8s Trust

Vault-Kubernetes Integration Step 10

⚠️ Prerequisites
Both Vault cluster and Kubernetes cluster must be fully deployed and operational. FluxCD must be bootstrapped.

What This Enables

Once complete, apps deployed on K8s can inject secrets from Vault directly into pods via the Vault Agent Injector.

Pod (with annotations)
        │
        ▼
   Vault Agent Injector
   (sidecar container)
        │
        ▼
   Authenticate via K8s SA
        │
        ▼
   Fetch secrets from Vault
        │
        ▼
   Inject at /vault/secrets/

Components

ComponentPurpose
vault-auth ServiceAccountK8s SA for Vault to verify pod identity
Vault Agent InjectorSidecar that injects secrets into pods
Kubernetes Auth MethodVault auth backend that trusts K8s SAs

The playbook will:

Per-Application Setup

For each new application that needs Vault secrets:

1
Run App Setup Script
On vault1
Setup Script 
ssh vault1.lab.local
./vault-pod-setup.sh

The script prompts for: Vault LDAP username, app name, K8s namespace, SA name, secret key/value pairs.

Creates in Vault:

  • Secret: secret/<app-name>/config
  • Policy: <app-name>-policy
  • K8s Role: <app-name>
2
Add Vault Annotations to Deployment
In your app deployment YAML
Deployment Annotations 
annotations:
  vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject: "true"
  vault.hashicorp.com/role: "<app-name>"
  vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-secret-config.txt: "secret/data/<app-name>/config"
  vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject-template-config.txt: |
    {{- with secret "secret/data/<app-name>/config" }}
    key1: {{ index .Data.data "key1" }}
    key2: {{ index .Data.data "key2" }}
    {{- end }}
  vault.hashicorp.com/tls-skip-verify: "false"
  vault.hashicorp.com/tls-secret: "vault-ca"
  vault.hashicorp.com/ca-cert: "/vault/tls/ca.crt"

spec:
  serviceAccountName: <app-name>-sa

Secrets available at: /vault/secrets/config.txt

Nginx Setup

What nginx_setup.yml Does

  • Installs Nginx via dnf
  • Deploys custom nginx.conf with upstream log format
  • Starts and enables Nginx service

Custom Log Format

We use a custom log format to show which K8s worker handled each request:

nginx.conf 
log_format upstream '$remote_addr - [$time_local] "$request" '
                    '$status $body_bytes_sent '
                    'upstream: $upstream_addr '
                    'response_time: ${request_time}s '
                    'upstream_time: ${upstream_response_time}s';

Site Configuration Template

nginx-test.conf.j2 
upstream k8s_workers {
    least_conn;
    server 10.0.64.10:30080;
    server 10.0.64.11:30080;
    server 10.0.64.12:30080;
}

server {
    listen 80;
    server_name nginx-test-dev.lab.local;

    access_log /var/log/nginx/nginx-test-dev.log upstream;

    location / {
        proxy_pass http://k8s_workers;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }
}

Apply Configuration

Apply Config 
ansible-playbook -i inventory/inventory.ini playbooks/nginx/apply_new_config.yml

Reference / Quick Commands

Quick Commands ⌨️

Kubernetes Commands

Cluster Status 
export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf

# Nodes
kubectl get nodes
kubectl get nodes -o wide

# Pods
kubectl get pods -A
kubectl get pods -n kube-system
kubectl get pods -n flux-system

# Services
kubectl get svc -A

# Calico
calicoctl node status

# Flux
flux get all
flux reconcile kustomization flux-system
HA Status 
systemctl status haproxy
systemctl status keepalived
ip addr show eth0 | grep 10.0.61.100

Vault Commands

Environment Setup 
export VAULT_ADDR="https://vault.lab.local:8200"
export VAULT_CACERT="/etc/ipa/ca.crt"
Status & Auth 
# Status
vault status

# Login
vault login -method=ldap username=<user>

# List mounts
vault secrets list
vault auth list

# K8s integration
vault read auth/kubernetes/config
vault list auth/kubernetes/role
Secrets 
# Read secret
vault kv get secret/<app>/config

# Update single key
vault kv patch secret/<app>/config key="value"

# Overwrite all
vault kv put secret/<app>/config key1="v1" key2="v2"

FreeIPA Commands

IPA Admin 
# Get Kerberos ticket
kinit admin
klist

# IPA status
ipactl status

# User management
ipa user-find
ipa user-show <username>
ipa group-find

# Host management
ipa host-find
ipa hostgroup-find

# DNS
ipa dnsrecord-find lab.local
Generate Keytab 
ipa-getkeytab -s freeipa.lab.local -p super_bot@LAB.LOCAL -k /tmp/super_bot.keytab
base64 /tmp/super_bot.keytab

VPN Commands

AWS EC2 
# WireGuard status
sudo wg show

# Service status
sudo systemctl status wg-quick@wg0
sudo systemctl status wg-keepalive

# Restart
sudo systemctl restart wg-quick@wg0

# Capture traffic
sudo tcpdump -i enX0 udp port 51820 -n
MikroTik 
/interface wireguard peers print
/interface wireguard peers print detail
/ping 172.16.200.2

Ansible Commands

Kerberos Auth 
# Get ticket for automation
kinit super_bot@LAB.LOCAL
klist
Run Playbooks 
cd ansible/dev/

# With first_setup_inventory (before domain join)
ansible-playbook -i inventory/first_setup_inventory.ini playbooks/...

# With main inventory (after domain join)
ansible-playbook -i inventory/inventory.ini playbooks/...

# Limit to specific hosts
ansible-playbook ... --limit k8s_masters
ansible-playbook ... --limit vault_cluster
Ansible Vault 
# View encrypted file
ansible-vault view inventory/group_vars/freeipa.yml

# Edit encrypted file
ansible-vault edit inventory/group_vars/freeipa.yml

# Decrypt inline variable
ansible-vault decrypt_string
